ops.title: Trust.Control on the FuseKit runtime must pin the CLI, not the app
ops.body:
Fixed in v0.65.1 (4a3881b). Recorded because the same mistake is easy to repeat, and
cc-pool's two sibling daemons already document the rule in comments this one missed.

`RuntimeTrust` (internal/holderbridge/plan.go) pinned `Controller` to `BundleID`
("com.yasyf.cc-pool.status"), the status app's identity. But the app drives its runtime
in process (holderbridge/process.go, the ProcessRuntime interface) and never opens a wire
session. The runtime's only Control peer is the Homebrew CLI, signed "com.yasyf.cc-pool".
daemonkit's internal/trust/verify.go:58 compares signing identifiers exactly, so the
daemon rejected the one caller the requirement exists to protect.

Symptom on a clean machine: `ccp package install` exits 1 at
"activate installed application: daemonkit: peer failed trust verification: wire: untrusted peer"
AFTER convergeAgents has written the app, registered the LaunchAgent, and started the job —
so `ccp init` and `ccp doctor` both report a healthy pool over an install that never sealed
activation.json. Nothing outside deploy's own idempotency compare reads that record, which
is why the runtime genuinely works.

The unrecoverable half: every subsequent install takes Supersede -> Quiesce, draining over
the same refused lane. deploy/quiesce.go's session-less fallback covers only ErrDraining and
ErrAbsent, so ErrUntrusted fails outright at "land packaged candidate". Upgrades were
unreachable on any machine that had installed 0.65.0. Reproduced on two independent
machines, one with no prior cc-pool state.

Three constraints that shaped the fix:
- Trust.Control is single-valued (daemonkit/daemon.go: Control *Requirement, while Business
  is Requirements where any element admits). A daemon structurally cannot admit two control
  identities; widening it needs a daemonkit change, and daemonkit is frozen at v0.21.4.
- The nil-floor that internal/daemon/spec.go and internal/tenantfs/product.go use is
  unavailable here: fusekit's holder/trust.go refuses an empty controller
  ("FuseKit runtime: control requirement is required").
- So the runtime pins the CLI identity, which internal/cli/release_artifact_contract_test.go
  already pins in CI — the two cannot drift.

Regression guard: plan_test.go asserts the controller requirement is NOT BundleID.
